Marissa —

Short answers below; I'll pull legal to review DPA redline but these are our standard positions: 

- Controller/Processor: Redwood's standard DPA states customers are Controllers and Redwood is a Processor for data sent to our API. We can include that clause in the redline.

- Subprocessors: we maintain a subprocessors registry and provide a current list on request. We notify customers of material changes via email and the registry. Link: https://www.redwood.ai/subprocessors (internal doc: SUBPROC-REG-2026).

- Breach notice: our standard is to provide notification of security incidents as soon as practicable and no later than 72 hours for incidents impacting customer PII. We will include that in the DPA; final legal review may caveat for law enforcement/forensics constraints.

- Logs and request bodies: default hosted behavior captures request metadata (timestamps, IP, model used, token counts) and — unless customer opts into debugging/logging — we do not retain full request bodies by default for production tenants. For customers who enable debugging or specific support sessions we may capture request bodies for a limited time.

- Retention: default request log retention is 30 days; embeddings retention defaults to 90 days unless configured. Customers can request custom retention windows for Dedicated/Private deployments.

- Data residency / BYOK: we offer EU-only regions for hosted deployments and support BYOK (KMS integration) for Dedicated and Private customers; for strict residency customers we recommend Redwood Private or a dedicated EU deployment.

Attaching current subprocessors list and will coordinate with Legal for the DPA redline.

Rgds,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Marissa / Rishi —

A few engineering specifics you can share with the customer: 

- Logging controls: production hosted tenants do not persist full request bodies by default. We capture metadata and provide an audit trail (request id, user id if provided, model, token counts, latency). Customers can enable full-body capture for short debugging windows and we provide UI + API controls to purge those logs.
- Redaction: we offer configurable PII redaction pipelines (regex-based and model-assisted) customers can apply at ingestion. This is recommended if customers will send sensitive PII fields.
- Retention & export: logs and artifacts can be exported via our console or via a secure S3 link for Dedicated/Private customers. For EU-only requirements we can pin to eu-central-1 region, and for extra control propose a BYOK KMS integration so keys are customer-managed.

I'll drop a small config snippet they can share with their security team.
